title: Gold Slips 1% as Markets Brace for US CPI Print
excerpt: Oil-driven inflation fears and a hawkish Fed have wiped 11% off gold since late February — Tuesday's CPI data could deepen the slide.
body:
Gold stumbled again on Monday, May 11, with spot prices falling 1% to $4,667.99 per ounce and June futures dropping 1.1% to $4,677.80 — as markets held their breath ahead of the most consequential inflation print of the year.

**What is driving the sell-off:**
Gold has shed more than 11% since the US-Israel strike on Iran in late February triggered an oil price surge that reignited inflation fears. Elevated crude prices feed directly into the Consumer Price Index, raising the likelihood of higher interest rates — and high rates are the single biggest weight on non-yielding bullion. The dollar rose Monday, making gold more expensive for holders of other currencies and compounding the pressure.

**Why Tuesday's CPI reading is the pivot point:**
Markets expect April CPI to rise 0.6% month-on-month — sharply lower than March's blistering 0.9% surge — with core CPI seen up 0.4%. A hotter-than-expected print would force traders to price in an even longer Fed pause, potentially extending the gold selloff further. Traders have already priced out virtually all Fed cuts this year; CME FedWatch now puts the probability of a rate hike by March 2027 at 31%. That sentiment triggered over $12.7 billion in North American gold ETF outflows in March 2026 alone — the largest monthly exodus in at least five years. Meanwhile, 30-year Treasury yields climbed back above 5.00%, their highest since July 2025, sharpening the opportunity cost of holding gold.

**What to watch next:**
All eyes land on the Bureau of Labor Statistics' April CPI release on Tuesday, May 12 — a cooler-than-expected reading could spark a short-covering rally, while any upside surprise threatens to push gold toward the $4,550 support zone that analysts are watching closely.
